quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #14
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 34

questions.question: When two vehicles enter an intersection from different roads at the same time, which vehicle must yield?
questions.explanation: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right when both arrive at an intersection at the same time.

questions.question: Motorcycles are entitled to:

options.text: The same full lane width as other motor vehicles.
Half the width of a lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same full lane width as other motor vehicles.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are entitled to use the same full lane width as all other vehicles.

questions.question: When driving in Idaho, you must:

options.text: Always drive at the maximum posted speed limit.
Drive at a speed that is reasonable and prudent at all times.
Drive 10 mph below the posted speed limit at all times.
Always drive at the same speed as the vehicles around you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive at a speed that is reasonable and prudent at all times.
questions.explanation: Idaho law requires you to drive at a safe speed for road and weather conditions. Slow down whenever conditions are not ideal for driving.

questions.question: If your wheels drop off the pavement onto the shoulder, you should:

options.text: Brake hard and turn sharply back onto the pavement.
Stop your car on the edge of the road.
Slow down and carefully turn back onto the pavement.
Maintain your speed and turn sharply back onto the pavement.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and carefully turn back onto the pavement.
questions.explanation: Reduce your speed without braking hard and carefully steer back onto the pavement. Check for other vehicles before re-entering the road.

questions.question: When dealing with pedestrians, a driver must:

options.text: Make sure the pedestrian is aware of their vehicle.
Always yield the right-of-way, even if the pedestrian is in the wrong.
Yield the right-of-way only when the pedestrian is legally entitled to it.
Slow down and sound their horn near a crosswalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always yield the right-of-way, even if the pedestrian is in the wrong.
questions.explanation: You must do everything possible to avoid hitting a pedestrian, no matter the circumstances. Always yield to pedestrians, even if they are crossing illegally.

questions.question: When riding in a vehicle, small children:

options.text: May be safely held by a strong adult.
Will be safe if they are standing on the floor in the back of the vehicle.
Will not be hurt in an accident because they are small.
Must never be allowed to ride while standing in the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must never be allowed to ride while standing in the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Children must always be in a proper child safety seat. No adult can safely hold a child during a crash. Never allow a child to stand or ride unrestrained.

questions.question: If a vehicle using high beams comes toward you, you should look toward ____ of the road.
questions.explanation: Look toward the right side of the road when an oncoming vehicle has high beams on. This prevents you from being blinded and helps you stay on your side of the road until the vehicle passes.

questions.question: What does a flashing yellow traffic light mean?
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means you should drive carefully and watch for hazards.

questions.question: How can you lower the risk of hydroplaning?

options.text: Do not speed when the roads are wet.
Use tires with proper air pressure.

questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when tires lose grip on wet roads. Reduce this risk by slowing down on wet roads, maintaining proper tire pressure, and replacing worn tires.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This warning sign tells you that a T intersection is coming. Be ready to turn right or left.

questions.question: If you are in an accident, what should you do?

options.text: Stop your vehicle at or near the accident scene.
Do not stand or walk in traffic lanes.
Turn off the engines of damaged vehicles.

questions.explanation: In an accident, stop at or near the scene. Move your vehicle out of traffic if possible. Do not stand or walk in traffic lanes—another vehicle could hit you. Turn off the engines of damaged vehicles.

questions.question: What should you do if traffic lights are not working due to a power outage?

options.text: Park your vehicle off the road and wait for power to return.
Use hand signals to show other drivers what you plan to do.
Turn on your hazard lights and drive through without stopping.
Treat it like a four-way stop sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Treat it like a four-way stop sign.
questions.explanation: When a traffic light is not working, treat the intersection like a four-way stop. Yield to other drivers the same way you would at a four-way stop. When it is your turn, go through carefully.

questions.question: When turning, you must ____ your speed.
questions.explanation: Slow down when turning. This helps you stay in control, keep in your lane, and react to unexpected situations.

questions.question: If two drivers arrive at the same time at a four-way stop sign intersection, who has the right-of-way?

options.text: One driver can go without stopping.
One driver should honk to show they are letting the other go.

questions.explanation: At a four-way stop, if you both arrive at the same time, give the right-of-way to the driver on your right. You may go when it is safe.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow line on your side of the center line mean?
questions.explanation: A solid yellow line next to your lane means you cannot pass other vehicles.

questions.question: You want to turn left at a multi-lane intersection, but oncoming traffic blocks your view. What should you do?

options.text: Go fast when the first lane clears.
Wait until you can see all the lanes you need to cross are clear, then turn.
Wait for an oncoming driver to wave you across.
Move your car into each lane as soon as traffic clears.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until you can see all the lanes you need to cross are clear, then turn.
questions.explanation: Never turn left until you can see that all the lanes you need to cross are clear and it is safe to turn.

questions.question: When must drivers yield to pedestrians?

options.text: Even if the pedestrian crosses carelessly.
Only when the pedestrian is in a crosswalk.
Only if the pedestrian is on the same side of the road.
Only if the pedestrian uses a hand signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Even if the pedestrian crosses carelessly.
questions.explanation: You must always yield to pedestrians in the street, even if they cross against the light or are being careless.

questions.question: If two drivers arrive at the same time at an open intersection with no traffic controls, who has the right-of-way?

options.text: One driver can go without stopping.
One driver should honk to show they are letting the other go.

questions.explanation: At an open intersection, if you both arrive at the same time, give the right-of-way to the driver on your right. You may go when it is safe.

questions.question: An oncoming vehicle is heading toward you in your lane. What should you do?

options.text: Honk, steer right, and speed up.
Stay in your lane, honk, and brake.

questions.explanation: If another vehicle is heading toward you, honk first to get their attention. If they do not move, steer right to escape. Steering left could cause a crash if they swerve at the last moment. Brake firmly and steadily. Every mile per hour you slow down reduces the impact.

questions.question: When passing a large vehicle in a small car, what should you be ready for?

options.text: Strong wind gusts from the large vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Strong wind gusts from the large vehicle.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles create strong wind gusts that can push smaller vehicles off course. Be ready to steer to stay safe when passing or being near large vehicles moving at high speeds.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.explanation: This is a regulatory sign. It tells drivers what they must do. This sign means right turns are not allowed.

questions.question: Another car is about to hit you. What should you do?
questions.explanation: Use your horn to warn other drivers or pedestrians who may not see you. If you think another driver is about to hit you, sound your horn.

questions.question: What does an orange sign mean?
questions.explanation: Orange signs with black symbols warn about construction, maintenance, and emergency work.

questions.question: How can you avoid hitting vehicles in your blind spots?

options.text: Turn your head and look over your shoulder before changing lanes.
Adjust your rearview mirrors every few minutes.
Honk your horn right before turning or changing lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look over your shoulder before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Before turning or changing lanes, turn your head and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Do not rely only on your mirrors.

questions.question: How should you handle a tailgater?

options.text: Speed up to increase the distance between you.
Brake hard to make them back off.
Change lanes or slow down gradually to let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes or slow down gradually to let them pass.
questions.explanation: Watch your mirrors to spot tailgaters. If a car is following too close, slow down gradually and let it pass. Most rear-end crashes happen because drivers follow too closely.

questions.question: What do downward-facing triangular signs mean?
questions.explanation: Downward-facing triangular signs tell drivers to yield. You must slow down and let other traffic pass before proceeding when it is safe.

questions.question: What do studies show about wearing a seat belt properly?

options.text: It increases your chance of dying in a crash.
It reduces damage to your car.
It reduces the risk of serious injury.

questions.correctAnswerText: It reduces the risk of serious injury.
questions.explanation: Studies show that seat belts greatly reduce your risk of serious injury in a crash. Seat belts prevent 60 to 70 percent of deaths in car crashes.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns that traffic is merging onto your road from the right.

questions.question: You are on a two-lane road with no bike lanes and see a bicyclist ahead. What is the safest way to pass?

options.text: Slow down, wait for oncoming traffic to clear, then pass while leaving plenty of space.
Drive straight. The bicyclist should get out of your way.
Wait until you reach a traffic light or stop sign before passing.
Honk to let the bicyclist know you are passing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, wait for oncoming traffic to clear, then pass while leaving plenty of space.
questions.explanation: Pass a bicyclist like you would pass any other vehicle. Leave at least 3 feet of space on normal roads and 5 feet on high-speed roads or when there are multiple bicyclists. Do not honk unnecessarily because it may startle riders and cause a crash.

questions.question: Before you start the engine, what should you do?

options.text: Make sure only backseat passengers have buckled their belts.
Make sure only adult passengers have buckled their belts.
Make sure only child passengers have buckled their belts.
Make sure all passengers have buckled their belts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure all passengers have buckled their belts.
questions.explanation: Develop a habit every time you get in your car. Before starting the engine, buckle your seat belt and make sure all passengers do the same.

questions.question: When a driver is turning and a pedestrian is crossing without a traffic light, who must yield?
questions.explanation: Drivers must always yield to pedestrians crossing at any intersection, even without a traffic light or crosswalk.

questions.question: What happens when you mix alcohol with drugs?
questions.explanation: Mixing alcohol and drugs increases the effects of both. It is dangerous to drive after using either one, and even more dangerous when you combine them.

questions.question: What should you do when you encounter an aggressive driver?

options.text: Avoid eye contact, slow down, and let them pass.
Cut them off to slow them down.
Make sure they know you disapprove.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid eye contact, slow down, and let them pass.
questions.explanation: If another driver is driving dangerously, stay calm and create distance between your cars. Slow down and let them pass. Do not make eye contact or make rude gestures.

questions.question: Your tire blows out while driving. What should you do?

options.text: Hold your steering wheel tightly and slow to a stop.
Turn on your emergency flashers and keep driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold your steering wheel tightly and slow to a stop.
questions.explanation: Do not brake suddenly. Grip the steering wheel firmly to stay in your lane. Gradually slow down by releasing the accelerator. Once you are moving slowly, gently apply the brakes and pull off the road safely.

questions.question: What size blind spots do larger vehicles have?
questions.explanation: The larger the vehicle, the larger its blind spots. Large trucks and SUVs have areas near their rear that cannot be seen in their mirrors.

questions.question: How can stress affect your driving?

options.text: It lowers your ability to focus on driving.
It decreases your chances of an accident.
It causes you to fall asleep at the wheel.
It makes you more aware of others around you.

questions.correctAnswerText: It lowers your ability to focus on driving.
questions.explanation: Emotions greatly affect your driving ability. Worry, anger, fear, or sadness can reduce your focus on driving. It is better to wait to drive until you feel emotionally stable.

questions.question: On a multilane, one-way street, which lane should you use to turn left?
questions.explanation: To turn left on multilane streets, start from the left lane.

questions.question: What color are signs for public recreation areas?
questions.explanation: Brown signs mark areas for public recreation or historical sites. They help travelers find these locations in unfamiliar areas.

questions.question: What does a green arrow on a traffic signal mean?

options.text: It is used only on one-way streets.
It means the same as a green light, but you must turn in the direction the arrow points.
You may proceed only if the arrow appears with a circular green light.
It points the way to an airport.

questions.correctAnswerText: It means the same as a green light, but you must turn in the direction the arrow points.
questions.explanation: A green arrow has the same meaning as a regular green light. However, traffic in that lane must turn in the direction shown by the arrow.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a flashing yellow light?

options.text: Slow down and proceed with caution.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with caution.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light warns of a hazard ahead. Slow down and proceed carefully.
